reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses Al-containing coatings on Zr alloys but focuses on AlNbTiZr medium-entropy alloys, not Cr-Al alloys, and does not demonstrate alumina formation at the coating-substrate interface or its effect on Cr-Zr interdiffusion. The key premises about alumina barrier formation and diffusion reduction in a Cr-Al system are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Aluminum addition to a Cr coating can form a protective alumina layer at the coating-substrate interface
This alumina layer reduces Cr-Zr interdiffusion by acting as a diffusion barrier
The Cr-Al alloy coating will maintain corrosion protection under normal and accident conditions
Aluminum preferentially oxidizes to form stable, adherent alumina
